summary: Paritok-4B is a 264 MB LoRA adapter on Qwen3-4B, distilled from a gpt-4.1-mini teacher over 67,074 OpenHands trajectories (SWE-rebench, SWE-Gym), that extractively compresses coding-agent context conditioned on the agent's current intent. On SWE-bench Lite (300 instances, single-shot, oracle file context, claude-sonnet-4-5 as solver) it compresses context to 25.7-27.8% of its size while retaining 86.5-89.3% of the uncompressed solve rate. The paired McNemar test is not significant (p=0.079). Released under Apache 2.0 by the company Paritok.

claims.claim: Compresses to 25.7% of size, 2.0x and 2.4x harder than gpt-4.1-mini (50.2%) and gpt-5 (61.9%) as compressors.
claims.evidence: Table 9 macro-averaged compression rates over 300 instances; corpus-level ratio 21.7% [20.0, 23.5]; per-instance IQR 15.2-35.3%.

claims.claim: Retains 86.5% (raw) / 89.3% (line-numbered) of uncompressed solve quality; not significantly worse.
claims.evidence: 122/300 uncompressed vs 109/300 compressed resolved; 30 vs 17 discordant, exact McNemar p=0.079; ratio paired bootstrap CI [79.2%, 100%]. The authors state 'not significant is not the same as no effect'. Apply failures 16 vs 5.

claims.claim: 96.0% of emitted identifiers/paths/numbers appear in its input (96.2% on held-out SWE-bench Lite).
claims.evidence: §3.1 extractiveness measurement over 64,843 emitted lines / 212,506 identifier-like tokens; audit scripts released. Roughly 60% of input identifiers are dropped (limitation 1).

claims.claim: gpt-5 as a compressor is net-negative at list prices; Paritok-4B's economics depend on self-hosting cost.
claims.evidence: Table 10: gpt-5 +$6.30 per 1M tokens vs raw; gpt-4.1-mini -$0.29; Paritok-4B wins only if C_self < $2.23/M (not measured). Uncached list pricing; caching would shrink savings.
Evaluation is single-shot with oracle file context, no agent loop, no tool calls, no exact-match edits; multi-turn agent effects deferred to a companion paper.
claims.location: §6.2 'What is and is not in the measured path', §7 limitation 7

patterns.note: Extractive, intent-conditioned compression keeps single-shot quality within noise at ~1/4 tokens, but apply failures triple and multi-turn agent behaviour is untested.
Explicit cost arithmetic shows a frontier-model compressor can cost more than it saves; useful budget reasoning.
Small self-hosted model for an auxiliary step, frontier model for solving; supports cheap-model routing for context processing.
SWE-bench Lite used in single-shot mode, not as an agentic benchmark.

methodology.sample: Training: 67,074 trajectories → 40,606 validated examples; evaluation: all 300 SWE-bench Lite instances plus an intrinsic OOD segment holdout.
methodology.baselines: Uncompressed; gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-5 as prompt-based compressors. No LLMLingua-family or other code-specific compressor baseline, and no agentic (multi-turn) baseline.
methodology.models: Compressor Qwen3-4B + LoRA; solver claude-sonnet-4-5 only (temperature 0).
methodology.variance: Wilson CIs, paired McNemar, bootstrap CIs on ratios and compression rate; single solver run.
methodology.ablations: Backbone selection (§5.1), drop-supervision weighting (§5.2, backfired), checkpoint sweep, line-numbered vs raw input.
methodology.contamination_controls: SWE-bench Lite held out from training; repo-level overlap between SWE-Gym/SWE-rebench training repos and SWE-bench Lite repos not checked.

standards.artifacts: Weights, data pipeline, SFT configs, audit scripts and SWE-bench harness at github.com/Paritok-official/paritok-4b-v1 (Apache 2.0) and Hugging Face.
standards.preregistration: n/a; reports a falsified prediction for the line-numbered regime.

biases.detail: Paritok company authors evaluate their own product with their own harness.
Training and evaluation on Python SWE-bench-style repos only.
Single-shot oracle-context patch generation is used to support claims about coding-agent context compression.
Training repos may overlap with SWE-bench Lite repositories; only the instances are held out.
Self-hosting throughput and cost (C_self) not measured, yet economics are a headline claim.

coi.affiliations: Jiayu Shi and Luzhuo Chen, Paritok (company email paritok9@gmail.com).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Paritok-4B, the authors' own product, compared favourably against gpt-4.1-mini/gpt-5 compressors.
coi.detail: Vendor evaluating its own product without independent replication. Mitigated by unusually candid statistics (non-significance, apply-failure counting, falsified prediction) and fully open artifacts.

verdict_reason: Statistically honest and fully open, with headline compression numbers in Table 9. But it is a vendor self-evaluation, Python-only, with a single solver, and the 'coding agent' claim rests on a single-shot harness with no agent loop and 3x more apply failures.
applicability: Moderate and indirect. For a Java team, the transferable ideas are: (1) any compression on the agent path must be extractive, with a byte-exact read_original fallback, because reflowed signatures break exact-match edits; (2) do the cost arithmetic before adding a paid-model compressor, which can cost more than it saves. The adapter itself is Python-tuned and unbenchmarked on Java. Repo invariants forbid placing a local LLM between the agent host and MCP servers, so a compressor gateway like this would have to be a host-side, opt-in component, not something qr runs. Mixed hosts with prompt caching will see smaller savings than Table 10.

conflicts_with.detail: Finds implicit (embedding) context compression works single-shot but fails on multi-step agentic coding tasks, a warning that Paritok's single-shot retention may not carry over to agent loops.
